What / How We Are Using It: Primary 100 MHz system clock driving the VeeR-EL2 CPU core, 2x8 AXI4 crossbar, DMA engine, CNN accelerator, Distance IP, and peripheral wrappers.
Primary system reset. When held low (0), resets all CPU pipeline registers, AXI bus arbiters, DMA FSM, and memory-mapped control registers to defaults.
Dedicated reset for on-chip RISC-V debug module and JTAG TAP controller; allows CPU reset without destroying active debug sessions.
Serial transmit wire to host PC/terminal. Transmits 26 structured ASCII log lines during boot, DMA transfer status, CNN embedding vectors, and final PASS banner.
Serial receive wire for external host commands or image data streaming into the SoC UART RX FIFO (held idle-high in simulation).
Physical status output pins. Driven by firmware to broadcast execution phases: 0x01 (CPU Boot Done), 0x02 (DMA Copy Done), 0x04 (CNN Inference Done), 0x55 (All Tests Passed).
External digital inputs connected to board switches, pushbuttons, or external trigger sensors; passed through an on-chip 2-stage synchronizer to prevent metastability.
Controls external bi-directional I/O pad buffers (1 = Output drive enabled, 0 = High-impedance / Input mode) based on the GPIO_EN configuration register.
Asserts high when DMA controller finishes a block transfer (e.g. 256-byte image copy from DMEM to CNN buffer); cleared synchronously via Write-1-to-Clear (W1C).
Asserts high when CNN hardware accelerator completes Conv3x3 -> ReLU -> MaxPool -> FC inference and valid 16-D embedding vector is ready in output registers.
Asserts high when Distance/Anomaly engine finishes Manhattan scoring and threshold comparison; signals valid RESULT (Match/Anomaly) and MIN_DISTANCE.
Asserts when UART transmitter FIFO is empty (THRE) or when incoming character bytes are available in the UART receiver FIFO.
Asserts when 64-bit real-time counter MTIME matches or exceeds programmed comparator threshold MTIMECMP; provides periodic RTOS/firmware tick.
Asserts when any enabled GPIO input pin detects a configured rising-edge, falling-edge, or level-sensitive transition.
External machine timer interrupt input wired into the VeeR-EL2 Programmable Interrupt Controller (PIC).
External inter-processor / software interrupt line routed to VeeR-EL2 PIC for multi-core IPC or OS rescheduling.
JTAG Test Clock input; clocks instruction register (IR) and data register (DR) scan chains for OpenOCD/GDB hardware debugging.
JTAG Test Mode Select; controls state machine transitions of the standard 16-state TAP controller.
JTAG Test Data In; serial data stream containing CPU debug commands, breakpoint registers, and memory access requests.
JTAG Test Reset; asynchronous hardware reset pin that resets TAP controller state to Test-Logic-Reset.
JTAG Test Data Out; serial data stream returning CPU register values, program counter, and debug status to host debugger.
Output driver enable control for external bi-directional JTAG TDO pad buffer (high only when TAP is in Shift-IR / Shift-DR state).
External hardware CPU halt request; forces VeeR-EL2 core to pause instruction fetch and pipeline for power saving or external debug control.
Acknowledge signal asserted by CPU when all outstanding load/store transactions finish and the pipeline has safely entered the halted state.
Continuous status flag indicating whether the VeeR-EL2 CPU core is currently halted.
External hardware CPU run request; resumes instruction fetching and execution for a previously halted CPU core.
Acknowledge signal asserted by CPU confirming that the core has successfully resumed active instruction execution.
Status output signal indicating that the RISC-V core is currently halted in debug mode under JTAG/DMI debugger control.
